home.title: Before You Paste
home.tagline: A browser practice lab and human-review training environment. A last check for text you are already allowed to use with an AI tool.
home.warning: This lab cannot make prohibited data permitted. If your organization's rules forbid putting beneficiary, protection or health information into AI tools, redaction does not change that.
home.sources: Sources: ICRC Handbook on Data Protection in Humanitarian Action; IASC Operational Guidance on Data Responsibility; OCHA Data Responsibility Guidelines (2025).
home.source.iasc: IASC Operational Guidance on Data Responsibility
home.privacy: Your text is not sent to a remote server. It stays in browser memory until you close the tab. Copying prepared text sends it to your operating system clipboard.
check.title: Check your text
check.instructions: Paste or type the text you plan to send to an AI chat tool. Run the check, then review every finding before you copy the prepared version.
check.inputTooLong: Text is too long ({length} characters). Maximum is {max} characters.
check.nerDescription: Optional layer: people, organizations and places using Xenova/distilbert-base-multilingual-cased-ner-hrl. Languages: 10 high-resource languages (Arabic, German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Latvian, Dutch, Portuguese and Chinese) per the model card.
check.nerFailed: Name recognition could not load. Pattern checks and context flags still run.
check.nerUnavailable: Name recognition unavailable. Pattern and context checks only.
check.patternOnly: Pattern and context checks only (name recognition off or unavailable)
check.modelPinned: Optional model pinned to revision {revision} (~{size} MB quantized download from Hugging Face). Hugging Face sees download requests, never your text.
permission.title: Before you scan
permission.intro: Answer these questions about the text you plan to check. The lab will not scan personal data unless your organization allows the tool and purpose.
permission.q1: Is this personal data about affected people, staff or volunteers?
permission.q2: Is the AI tool approved by your organization for this kind of information?
permission.q3: Is this purpose allowed under your organization's rules?
permission.blocked: The lab will not scan this text. Personal data requires an approved tool and an allowed purpose under your organization's rules.
permission.needAnswer: Please answer whether the text is personal data before continuing.
permission.contact: Contact your organization's data-protection focal point. See:
review.title: Review findings
review.instructions: Each finding has a label and icon. Choose replace, generalize or keep. You can also select missed text and add a finding.
review.noFindings: No findings yet. Run a check or add items manually.
review.contextNote: Review the context: this term is sensitive. The lab never auto-removes context flags.
review.notAnonymous: Placeholders do not make data anonymous or permitted.
review.recallLoadFailed: Measured recall figures could not be loaded.
output.title: Prepared text
output.copyFailed: Clipboard copy failed. Select and copy the text below manually.
output.namesNotChecked: Names of people, organizations and places were not checked.
output.invariantError: "{text}" is still present in the prepared text.
output.invariantBlocked: Copy is blocked until every replaced or generalized item is removed from the prepared text.
restore.title: Restore original details
restore.instructions: Paste the AI tool's reply below. The lab restores your original details locally. Placeholders the reply changed, merged or invented are flagged. Placeholders the reply does not use are listed for information.
restore.issue.invented: Placeholder invented by AI (not in your mapping)
restore.info.unused: Not used in the reply (information only)
restore.reviewInstructions: Compare each line. Placeholders the AI changed, merged or invented are flagged. Placeholders the reply does not use are listed for information.
restore.confirmLabel: I have reviewed the comparison and accept the restored text.
restore.noIssues: No placeholder issues detected (detection is incomplete).
restore.cleared: All text and mappings cleared from memory.
restore.noMap: No placeholder mapping in memory. Prepare text first.
mosaic.warning: Several details together may identify someone without a full name (mosaic effect).
mosaic.source: Sources: Centre for Humanitarian Data mosaic effect glossary; Exploring the Mosaic Effect on HDX; Statistical Disclosure Control guidance.
mosaic.groupRisk: This may also identify a specific group in a small population.
mosaic.pair.ageLocation: Combining {items} can narrow to a few individuals in a camp or village.
mosaic.pair.ageSex: Combining {items} can identify someone in a small group.
mosaic.pair.roleLocation: Combining {items} can identify staff or beneficiaries in a small site.
mosaic.pair.roleAge: Combining {items} can single out individuals in programme records.
mosaic.pair.dateLocation: Combining {items} can identify who was present.
mosaic.pair.groupMatch: Combining {items} may identify a specific group in a small population.
context.health: Health or disability information can be especially sensitive in humanitarian contexts.
context.gbv: Sexual and gender-based violence information requires strict protection.
context.children: Child protection information needs heightened safeguards.
context.ethnicity: Ethnicity can increase targeting risk when combined with location.
context.religion: Religion can be sensitive in conflict-affected areas.
context.political: Political opinion may put people at risk.
context.sogi: Sexual orientation and gender identity may be criminalized or stigmatized.
context.migration: Migration or legal status can affect safety and access to services.
context.criminal: Criminal allegations require careful handling and may be unverified.
context.biometrics: Biometric data is highly identifying and often specially regulated.

risk.brief: Browser extensions with page access can read text boxes. Use a private window with extensions off.

why.title: Why this matters
why.p1.title: Data minimization
why.p1.text: Share only what the task needs. The ICRC Handbook and IASC guidance stress collecting and using the minimum data necessary.
why.p2.title: Purpose limitation
why.p2.text: Use data only for the stated humanitarian purpose. OCHA guidelines remind teams to define purpose before sharing or analysing data.
why.p3.title: Mosaic effect
why.p3.text: Combined small details can identify people without names. The Centre for Humanitarian Data describes this as the mosaic effect: separate non-identifying fields can become identifying when combined.
why.p4.title: Consent and power imbalance
why.p4.text: Affected people may not freely refuse data use. ICRC guidance highlights dignity and accountability when processing personal data.
why.p5.title: Organizational rules first
why.p5.text: Your agency's policies and approvals override any tool. UNESCO and ICRC AI policies stress human control and organizational accountability.
limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.text: This lab may miss nicknames, unusual spellings, transliterated names and indirect identifiers. Word lists are not exhaustive. The model can be wrong in either direction. This is not a compliance or anonymization guarantee. A person must review every result.
